dietary.title: Before you add dietary and allergy details
dietary.collected: Your dietary needs, allergies and dietary notes, and any meal preference you give on a project. These can reveal your health or your religion.
dietary.why: So a production you choose to share them with can feed you safely. We use them for nothing else, and no AI feature reads them.
dietary.who: You. If you share this category with a project, these people also see them: that organization's Owner, the catering lead and on-site medical roles on that project, and anyone else the organization gives medical data access there. Each read shows in your access log. A meal preference you give on a project goes to those same people on that project. Other people there see these details locked. Catering planners see counts of five or more people, with no names. Your company cannot read them. If it enters your meal preference, it cannot read it back, you are told, and you can remove it.
dietary.withdraw: Withdraw under Work Details at any time, in one step. We stop using the details at once and delete them. If a legal hold reaches your data, we keep them hidden until the hold ends, then delete them.
dietary.attest: Someone is entering this for another person. Enter it only if that person asked you to or agreed, and has been told what is entered, why and who sees it. They can have it removed at any time.
dietary.attestCollected: The guest's dietary needs, allergies and dietary notes. These can reveal their health or religion.
dietary.attestWhy: So the production can feed the guest safely. They are used for nothing else, and no AI feature reads them.
dietary.attestWho: On this project, the organization's Owner, the catering lead and on-site medical roles, and anyone else the organization gives medical data access there, each read logged. Whoever keeps the guest list sees only who attested and when. They are deleted when the guest is removed or declined, and at the latest 90 days after the project ends.
dietary.attestAuthority: I have this person's authority to enter this.
dietary.attestNotice: This person has been told what is entered, why and who sees it, and that they can have it removed.
dietary.mealTitle: Enter a meal preference for this person
dietary.mealBody: A meal preference can reveal health or religion. It is optional, and it is used only to feed them on this project. No AI feature reads it.
dietary.mealWho: On this project, the organization's Owner, the catering lead and on-site medical roles, and anyone else the organization gives medical data access there read it, each read logged. Once it is saved, your company cannot read it back. The person is told and can remove it.

accessibility.title: Before you add accessibility details
accessibility.collected: Your accessibility needs and notes. These can reveal a disability or a health condition.
accessibility.why: So a production you choose to share them with can plan for you and get you out safely. We use them for nothing else, and no AI feature reads them.
accessibility.who: You. If you share this category with a project, these people also see them: that organization's Owner, the catering lead and on-site medical roles on that project, and anyone else the organization gives medical data access there. Each read shows in your access log. Other people there see them locked. Your company cannot read them.
accessibility.withdraw: Withdraw under Work Details at any time, in one step. We stop using the details at once and delete them. If a legal hold reaches your data, we keep them hidden until the hold ends, then delete them.
accessibility.attest: Someone is entering this for another person. Enter it only if that person asked you to or agreed, and has been told what is entered, why and who sees it. They can have it removed at any time.
accessibility.attestCollected: The guest's accessibility needs and notes. These can reveal a disability or a health condition.
accessibility.attestWhy: So the production can plan for the guest and get them out safely. They are used for nothing else, and no AI feature reads them.
accessibility.attestWho: The same people, on the same terms, as dietary needs: the Owner, the catering lead and on-site medical roles on this project, and anyone else the organization gives medical data access there, each read logged, and deleted at the same times.
accessibility.attestAuthority: I have this person's authority to enter this.
accessibility.attestNotice: This person has been told what is entered, why and who sees it, and that they can have it removed.

diversity.title: Before you add a supplier diversity certification
diversity.collected: The kind of certification, the certifying body, its number and its dates. This can reveal race, sex, sexual orientation, disability or veteran status.
diversity.why: So an organization that runs a supplier diversity program can count it, if you choose to share it with them. We use it for nothing else, and no AI feature reads it.
diversity.who: You, or the Owners and Admins of the company it belongs to. If you share it with an organization, the members there with restricted data access also see it, and each read shows in your access log.
diversity.withdraw: Withdraw here at any time, in one step. We stop using it at once, end every share and remove it. If a legal hold reaches your data, we keep it hidden until the hold ends, then remove it.
diversity.attest: You are declaring this for a company. Do it only if you have authority to speak for the company, and the people it describes have been told what is declared, why and who sees it.
diversity.attestAuthority: I have authority to declare this for the company.
diversity.attestNotice: The people it describes have been told what is declared, why and who sees it.

about.title: Entered for you by someone else
about.description: Someone said they had your authority to enter these. Remove anything you did not agree to: whoever entered it cannot enter it for you again, by your account or email, anywhere in that organization, and nobody can on that guest list entry, until you agree to it yourself. If a guest list entry is about someone else, choose This is not me instead: your name and email come off it, and the guest's needs stay with whoever keeps the list.
